function_v0.doc:
This card's purse, or `None` when no factory is configured or no purse has been
deployed yet.

The one link an outside reader cannot reconstruct alone: `public_key(token_id)`
is public, but nothing on chain says which factory to ask. Deliberately a
*pointer* and not a balance \xe2\x80\x94 the purse holds the card's float and its DeFi
positions, and it can answer for both without this contract mirroring either.

Best-effort by design: a missing, mis-pointed or trapping factory reads as
`None`. Resolving a card must never be able to fail because of a contract this
one merely points at.

# Arguments

* `e` - The environment object.
* `token_id` - Token id as a number.

# Returns

The purse address, or `None`.

# Panics

* If the token does not exist (`NonFungibleTokenError::NonExistentToken`).
function_v0.name: pocket

function_v0.doc:
Set a stored trait. Admin only.

# Arguments

* `e` - The environment object.
* `token_id` - Token id as a number.
* `trait_key` - Name of the trait; only `tier` exists.
* `new_value` - The value to store.

# Panics

* If the admin does not authorize the call.
* If the token does not exist (`NonFungibleTokenError::NonExistentToken`).
* If the key is not a declared trait (`NonFungibleTokenError::TraitDoesNotExist`).

# Events

Two, in this order:

* topics - `["set_trait", token_id: u32]`, data - `{trait_key: String, new_value:
i128}`. SEP-50's trait update.
* topics - `["metadata"]`, data - `token_id: u32`. SEP-50's metadata update, because
`tier` drives the art, so a new value means the metadata a client cached is stale.
Mint does not emit it: nothing is cached yet.
function_v0.name: set_trait

function_v0.doc:
Value of one trait, or `0` for a known trait that has never been set (the
standard's default). An unknown key is an error, not a zero.

# Arguments

* `e` - The environment object.
* `token_id` - Token id as a number.
* `trait_key` - Name of the trait; only `tier` exists.

# Returns

The stored value, or `0` if none was set.

# Panics

* If the token does not exist (`NonFungibleTokenError::NonExistentToken`).
* If the key is not a declared trait (`NonFungibleTokenError::TraitDoesNotExist`).
function_v0.name: trait_value

function_v0.doc:
Values of several traits of one token, in the order the keys were given.

# Arguments

* `e` - The environment object.
* `token_id` - Token id as a number.
* `trait_keys` - At most 32 trait names.

# Returns

One value per key, as [`NFCtoNFT::trait_value`] returns it.

# Panics

* If more than 32 keys are given (`NonFungibleTokenError::TooManyTraitKeys`).
* Whatever [`NFCtoNFT::trait_value`] panics on, for any key.
function_v0.name: trait_values

function_v0.doc:
Where the ERC-7496 trait schema lives.

# Arguments

* `e` - The environment object.

# Returns

The schema location, or an empty string if none was set.
function_v0.name: trait_metadata_uri

function_v0.doc:
Admin-set, so the schema can be republished without an upgrade. Emits, because
the schema is what tells a reader how to interpret every value it has cached.

# Arguments

* `e` - The environment object.
* `uri` - The new location of the trait schema.

# Panics

* If the admin does not authorize the call.

# Events

* topics - `["set_trait_metadata_uri"]`
* data - `{uri: String}`
function_v0.name: set_trait_metadata_uri

function_v0.doc:
Stateless chip-signature oracle over the registry's stored curve. Replay is the
caller's digest contract: callers must put their own nonce/expiry inside
`digest` (the Pocket passes the host authorization payload; attestation
integrators bring a domain + nonce). Unknown cards verify false.

udt_union_v0.doc:
What the holder wants to happen when this purse needs new code. Here rather than in
`pocket` because the factory passes it to the Pocket constructor and a `cdylib` cannot
be a library dependency.

**Enforced on the purse, recorded on the account.**

For a purse this decides how the contract holds its code. `Managed` deploys an
executable *reference* to the factory's entry, so one `set_pocket_wasm_hash` re-points
the whole fleet at once; `Pocket::upgrade` refuses under it, because pinning a hash
would leave the fleet in silence. `Manual` pins a hash that only the card's own chip
can move. That is CAP-85, and it is the second authority a gate always needed \xe2\x80\x94 the
tag owner \xe2\x80\x94 which is why this stopped being a note and became a decision.

`ChimpAccount` still only records it: accounts are deployed off-chain by a G-address,
so nothing owns an entry for them to reference.
